title: The Dead Salmons of AI Interpretability
abstract: arXiv:2512.18792v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: In a striking neuroscience study, the authors placed a dead salmon in an MRI scanner and showed it images of humans in social situations. Astonishingly, standard analyses of the time reported brain regions predictive of social emotions. The explanation, of course, was not supernatural cognition but a cautionary tale about misapplied statistical inference. In AI interpretability, reports of similar "dead salmon" artifacts abound: feature attribution, probing, sparse auto-encoding, and even causal analyses can produce plausible-looking explanations for randomly initialized neural networks. Upon inspection of this phenomenon our position is to argue for a pragmatic statistical-causal reframing: explanations of computational systems should be treated as parameters of a (statistical) model, inferred from computational traces. translated_abstract: 在一项引人注目的神经科学研究中，作者将一条死鲑鱼放入MRI扫描仪中，并向其展示人类社交情境的图像。令人惊讶的是，当时的标准分析竟报告出与社会情绪相关的脑区。当然，其解释并非超自然的认知，而是一个关于错误应用统计推断的警示故事。在AI可解释性领域，类似的“死鲑鱼”伪影现象大量存在：特征归因、探测、稀疏自编码，甚至因果分析都可能为随机初始化的神经网络生成看似合理的解释。在考察这一现象后，我们的立场是主张一种务实的统计-因果重构：对计算系统的解释应被视为（统计）模型的参数，从计算轨迹中推断得出。这一视角超越了仅仅测量由有限采样导致的解释统计变异性……
tldr: 该论文借神经科学中著名的“死鲑鱼”事件警示当前AI可解释性方法（如特征归因、探测、稀疏自编码）可能对随机初始化的神经网络生成虚假解释，并提出应将解释视为从计算轨迹中推断的统计模型参数这一统计-因果重构框架。
en_tdlr: Drawing on the famous "dead salmon" neuroscience cautionary tale, this paper warns that AI interpretability methods such as feature attribution, probing, and sparse auto-encoding can produce spurious explanations for randomly initialized networks, and proposes reframing explanations as parameters of a statistical model inferred from computational traces.
